title: Changing Items
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to replace a value that is already in a list by assigning to an index.
learn: Change an item with list[index] = value
idea: Lists can change after you create them. To replace one item, put the index on the left side of the =, like scores[1] = 95. That swaps only that one spot, and the rest of the list stays exactly the same.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change scores[1] = 85 to scores[1] = 99 and press Run. The middle number should become 99.

practice.text: Change the second color to "purple" and print the list.
practice.hint: The second item is index 1 and not 2. Assign a new string to that spot with colors[1] = ...
practice.starterTip: Add colors[1] = "purple" between the comment and print(colors).
practice.gradingNote: Pass if colors[1] is set to "purple" and the list is printed.

practice.text: Fix the typo: change "appple" to "apple" using an index assignment, then print.
practice.hint: The misspelled word is the first item, so use index 0 on the left side of the = to replace it.
practice.starterTip: Write fruit[0] = "apple" under the comment, then run print(fruit).
practice.gradingNote: Pass if fruit[0] becomes "apple" via assignment and the list is printed.

quiz.question: What does names[0] = "Sam" do?

options.text: Replaces the first item with Sam

quiz.correct: Right, assigning to an index replaces that item.
quiz.wrong: list[index] = value changes that one spot.

quiz.question: After nums = [1, 2, 3] and nums[2] = 9, what is nums?
quiz.correct: Yes, index 2 is the third item, so it becomes 9.
quiz.wrong: Index 2 is the last item in a list of three.

quiz.question: Does changing one index change the other items?

options.text: Only if the list is empty

quiz.correct: Right, only the index you assign to gets replaced.
quiz.wrong: The other positions keep their old values.
